decisions.reason: The original universal claim fails for S={s}, two self-looping actions, and a deterministic expert: one demonstration (s,pi*(s)) labels every state reachable by any learner. This is a logic defect in the Definition, not a dependency-citation error. Replaced only the final sentence with the coverage caveat; fixed demonstrations may omit learner-visited states, but covered labels can be reused without new expert interaction.

reviews.reason: Reviewed the complete Definition, its three prerequisite interfaces, owning boundary contract and both page inventories. Nonempty finite S, T>=1, normalized occupancy, deterministic expert, bounded disagreement-dominating surrogate, attained minimum and online timing are coherent. Corrected only the false label-necessity sentence; all formulas and hypotheses are preserved. This is the repair author’s review, not an independent review of the repair.

downstream_uses.alg-dagger: Definition steps 1–4 use the unchanged mixed policy, expert label and round-loss interfaces. Querying every visited state is an explicit instruction of this particular procedure, so requiring an interactive expert here is sound even if some queries could be replaced by cached labels.
downstream_uses.lem-dagger-mixture-occupancy: Statement and F1/steps 1.1–3.1 use only the unchanged occupancy recursion and per-decision mixture. The residual-mass argument never assumes missing labels or compulsory new expert interaction.
downstream_uses.lem-dagger-task-cost-from-expert-surroga: Statement and F1/steps 1.1–4.1 use unchanged J, Q*, V*, occupancy and disagreement domination. The hybrid-policy telescoping bound depends on those numerical quantities, independently of how expert labels were obtained.
downstream_uses.ex-behavior-cloning-covariate-shift: Example and F1/steps 1.1–3.1 compare unchanged expert and learner occupancies and disagreement loss. This specific model has an uncovered bad state b, so the distribution-shift witness remains valid. Its four diagram arrows and action/cost labels agree with the specified transitions.
downstream_uses.ex-dagger-interactive-expert-labels: Example and F1/F2/steps 1.1–3.1 use unchanged expert labels and the specified DAgger queries. Every expert-only rollout from g stays at g, whereas the first bad-learner rollout reaches b, so this example really does lack demonstration coverage at b. Both training labels yield the claimed unique minimizer. Diagram transitions, start arrow and action/cost labels agree with the text.
downstream_uses.ex-surrogate-loss-fails-task-cost-contro: Example and F1/steps 1.1–2.1 use only unchanged disagreement and task cost. Both policies have point-mass occupancy at s; the zero candidate score fails domination because learner disagreement is one. Its two diagram loops carry the correct distinct costs. This is also a concrete one-state setting where one expert label covers all visited states.
downstream_uses.thm-dagger-no-regret-reduction: Statement explicitly runs the population-loss DAgger procedure; its interaction sentence specifies that protocol, rather than asserting that every possible imitation-learning instance lacks demonstration coverage. F1/F2 and proof steps 1.1, 2.1–4.1 use unchanged loss, occupancy, mixture and task-cost formulas. Allowing cached labels in covered instances invalidates none of those inequalities; no necessary consumer repair follows.
downstream_uses.thm-dagger-finite-sample-generalization: Statement runs finite-trajectory DAgger and explicitly assumes the conditional rollout-mean identity. F1/F2 and proof steps 1.1–4.1 use unchanged true/empirical losses and occupancies. Label coverage does not alter those assumptions or the centered trajectory-loss increments, so the supplier correction leaves this argument sound.
